method.label: Use a sloping base and altitude

annotationRationale: The method finds the vertices by intersecting lines, calculates the base and altitude with coordinate distances, and applies the triangle area formula. Point-slope form and perpendicular slopes support those steps.
sourceMethod: Followed the first official solution using the side on x+y=10 as the base. Made the intersection calculations and the construction of the altitude foot explicit.

review.mathCheck: The lines are \(y=x/2+1\) and \(y=2x-2\), meeting the base at \((6,4)\) and \((4,6)\). The perpendicular foot is \((5,5)\), inside that segment. Base \(2\sqrt2\) and height \(3\sqrt2\) give area 6, choice C.
review.sourceMethodCheck: Faithful, originally worded expansion of MAA 10A Solution 7, printed pages 3 and 4. The vertices and perpendicular altitude agree with the official figure.
review.annotationCheck: The line equations, intersections, perpendicular foot and lengths are reconstructible without a diagram. No point-to-line distance formula is required.

nativeLayerJudgments.CN: Exact links fit point-slope form, intersections, coordinate distance and triangle area. The accepted partial slope link is demonstrated for finite perpendicular slopes; parallel, coincident and vertical-line cases are unassessed.
nativeLayerJudgments.US: 8.G.B.8 and the triangle-area component of G-GPE.B.7 are demonstrated. G-GPE.B.5 supports perpendicular-line construction, without proving slope criteria; G-GPE.B.4 supplies limited coordinate-reasoning overlap. The 6.G.A.1 link overlaps in triangle area, but its composition/decomposition technique is not demonstrated. These do not establish full coverage of the broader standards.
nativeLayerJudgments.ailleo: Assessed cnm_h172, cnm_h173 and cnm_p148 match intersections, distances and area. Supporting cnm_h169 and cnm_h168 match point-slope equations and perpendicular slopes. All five direct nodes are appropriate.
